Definition: from G3844 and the alternate of G4482; to flow by, i.e. (figuratively) carelessly pass (miss):--let slip.
BiblicalUsage: Pararrheo means to flow by, to drift past, to let slip. It appears once, in Hebrews 2:1, where we are told to give the more earnest heed to the things we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip. The Greek text spells this word pararrheo; the site's spelling is the same verb under its Strong's form.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe truth drifts away from people who stop holding it, and the warning in Hebrews is for me: pay attention, or the gospel will slip past like water.
